mechanism_narrative: A quarterly GDP growth rate (GDPC1) above 15000 billion dollars indicates robust economic expansion, directly increasing corporate earnings expectations and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to sustained profit growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 > 15000, or the correlation coefficient between GDPC1 and 20-day returns is < 0.05 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.10% signals ultra-low interest rates that reduce equity discount rates and increase risk appetite, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days as capital flows into equities.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.10, or the average return is not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates labor market tightening, boosting consumer spending and corporate margins, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when UNRATE falls > 0.2pp and PAYEMS rises > 50k, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing production (INDPRO) above 104.0 indicates strong industrial output, which accelerates inventory turnover and profit growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days during stable inflation regimes.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when INDPRO > 104.0 and CPIAUCSL < 2.5% YoY, or the return effect is insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: CPIAUCSL above 235.0 indicates moderate inflation consistent with economic growth, reducing recession fears and supporting positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days through sustained market confidence.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 235.0, or the return correlation is < 0.03 (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 1000 thousand units signals strong residential construction, directly increasing consumer wealth and spending, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 1000, or the return effect is not significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Manufacturing production (INDPRO) below 100.0 indicates industrial contraction, triggering recession concerns that reduce equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 55% of instances when INDPRO < 100.0, or the return effect is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 0.50% during monetary tightening cycles increases discount rates and reduces equity attractiveness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in > 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 0.50, or the return effect is insignificant (p > 0.05).
